headline: Red Sox find a spark in Detroit while Roman Anthony heads home
morning_brew: Monday night in Detroit finally gave us something to cheer about after that miserable stretch at Fenway Park. Payton Tolle was absolutely dealing, giving up just one hit over seven innings of work. Five runs in the seventh inning turned the whole game around, capped off by that massive three-run blast from Jarren Duran. It is about time this offense showed some life because we have been starving for a performance like this.

The win comes with a side of worry as Roman Anthony is heading back to the Hub to get his hand checked out. Losing a young talent like that right when the team is trying to climb out of the basement is absolutely brutal. I been watchin' this team since '78, and the injury bug always seems to bite at the worst possible moment. We need that kid in the lineup if we are going to make any noise in the AL East.

Around the rest of the Hub, it is a lot of waiting and wondering. The Celtics and Bruins are both facing long summers of what-ifs after those early exits at the Garden. Over in the legal world, the Stefon Diggs trial is getting underway. It is a tough situation for everyone involved, so we should just hope for a fair process and let the league handle the details. If a suspension comes down later, we will see how it affects the roster in Foxborough.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox's Roman Anthony to have hand rechecked in Boston
news_digest.dans_take: Total heartbreaker for the kid, hope the news is better than it sounds once he gets home.

news_digest.headline: Stefon Diggs' attorney says assault never happened as trial begins
news_digest.dans_take: Hope everyone is safe, but we will let the league and the courts sort this one out.

news_digest.headline: Brenda Song, Macaulay Culkin lead NBA playoffs celebrity sightings
news_digest.dans_take: I do not care who is sitting courtside if the Celtics are not on the floor.
